headline: High-risk write and workflow interaction: Dify can mutate shared files and execute shell/subprocesses while Airflow can egress broadly, creating dangerous default-path conflicts and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between Airflow and Dify, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Dify can read/write files and run tools, and Airflow can emit API-driven outputs; if operators bridge them via files or copied prompts, malicious content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is unusual, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airflow output into a Dify prompt or file
IF Dify ingests Airflow-generated text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Use a strict handoff template for any copied text
Add a visible delimiter around untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge base content, and model-provider/tool credentials, while Airflow has broad network egress. If Airflow outputs are placed into Dify’s shared workspace or prompts, sensitive content can flow into Dify and then out through provider calls. The shared-data pathway is plausible in default deployments, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are copied into Dify knowledge-base files or conversation context
IF Dify routes that content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Restrict Dify projects to non-sensitive inputs
Turn off ingestion of Airflow logs into Dify
Separate credentials used by each system
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and Dify can execute shell/subprocesses and write the filesystem. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared resources if co-located, and Dify’s per-conversation shared datastore increases collision risk. The overlap is dangerous by default when pointed at the same workspace or APIs.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or datastore
IF Airflow tasks and Dify tools target the same external API or file path

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify’s agent/workflow tooling can treat upstream text as actionable input, while Airflow can generate operational outputs that downstream systems may trust. If Airflow-produced facts are fed into Dify without verification, Dify can amplify a bad assumption into tool calls or workflow actions. That default-path cascade can cause irreversible operational mistakes.
conditions: IF Airflow output is used as authoritative input to a Dify workflow
IF Dify tool calls are enabled on that workflow
mitigations: Require schema validation on Airflow outputs
Log and diff upstream facts before action

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and model-provider API keys, while Airflow’s profile shows no data classes touched. If regulated data is routed into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Airflow’s handling. The other agent is not cited for a residency mismatch because its profile lacks a specific jurisdiction claim.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF Dify retention settings exceed the organization’s policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Dify
Review provider DPA and residency settings
